units.text: The Louisiana Purchase price was $15 million paid to France in 1803, but the negotiators were authorized to pay up to $10 million for New Orleans only. The final price exceeded the New Orleans budget/authorization.

citations.title: The Actual Louisiana Purchase Price - JSTOR Daily

judgement.reason: The passages support the $15 million price paid in 1803 and the $10 million authorization, but describe the authorization as for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas, not New Orleans only.

units.text: The $15M total purchase price was greater than the negotiators' $10M authorization for New Orleans and Floridas; no source supports that it fell below that budget.

judgement.reason: Both passages state negotiators were authorized up to $10 million for New Orleans/Floridas and agreed to $15 million for all Louisiana, so the price was greater and neither passage suggests it fell below the authorization.

units.text: The $15M purchase price did not fall below the negotiators' New Orleans budget; evidence consistently shows the final price surpassed the $10M authorization.

citations.title: Louisiana Purchase | Definition, Date, Cost, History, Map, States, Significance, & Facts | Britannica

judgement.reason: The National Archives passage states negotiators were authorized up to $10 million for New Orleans and the Floridas but agreed to $15 million for the entire territory, so the purchase price did not fall below and exceeded that authorization.
